titlePl: Ósmoklasista: Żywienie — 36 haseł do gier LingoSpark
titleEn: Grade 8 English: Food & Eating — 36 terms for LingoSpark games
blurbPl: Gotowa lista na dział Żywienie (egzamin ósmoklasisty). Wklejasz do Bomb Defusal, fiszek, Grid Territory, Vocab Auction albo Live Quiz na LingoSpark — plus karty pracy do druku.
blurbEn: A ready Grade-8 exam list for Food & Eating. Paste into Bomb Defusal, Flashcards, Grid Territory, Vocab Auction or Live Quiz on LingoSpark, plus printable worksheets.

items.definitionEn: a way of eating that includes a healthy mix of different foods
items.example: A balanced diet includes fruit, vegetables and some protein.

items.definitionEn: unhealthy food that is high in fat, sugar or salt
items.example: Too much junk food can make you feel tired after school.

items.definitionEn: a sweet drink with bubbles of gas in it
items.example: She ordered a fizzy drink with her pizza.

items.definitionEn: water with bubbles of gas in it
items.example: I prefer sparkling water to still water with dinner.

items.definitionEn: water without bubbles of gas
items.example: Could we have a bottle of still water, please?

items.definitionEn: food made from milk, such as cheese or yoghurt
items.example: If you are allergic to dairy, avoid cheese and cream.

items.definitionEn: birds kept for meat or eggs, such as chicken or turkey
items.example: Roast poultry is a popular Sunday meal in Britain.

items.definitionEn: animals from the sea that people eat, such as fish and prawns
items.example: The restaurant is famous for fresh seafood.

items.definitionEn: made from the whole grain, not just the white part
items.example: Wholemeal bread is healthier than white bread.

items.definitionEn: a person who does not eat meat; food with no meat
items.example: There is always a vegetarian option on the menu.

items.definitionEn: the foods you need to cook a particular dish
items.example: Check the ingredients before you start cooking.

items.definitionEn: a set of instructions for cooking a dish
items.example: This recipe for apple cake is easy to follow.

items.definitionEn: a small dish eaten at the beginning of a meal
items.example: We had tomato soup as a starter.

items.definitionEn: the largest part of a meal, usually with meat or a hot dish
items.example: The main course was grilled chicken with rice.

items.definitionEn: sweet food eaten at the end of a meal
items.example: Would you like dessert, or just coffee?

items.definitionEn: a meal you buy and take home to eat
items.example: We ordered a Chinese takeaway on Friday night.

items.definitionEn: food remaining after a meal, often eaten later
items.example: We had leftovers from Sunday lunch on Monday.

items.definitionEn: to reserve a place in a restaurant in advance
items.example: You should book a table if you go out on Saturday.

items.definitionEn: the piece of paper that shows how much you must pay
items.example: Could we have the bill, please?

items.definitionEn: extra money you leave for the waiter
items.example: In Britain people often leave a ten percent tip.

items.definitionEn: cooked in hot water
items.example: Boiled potatoes are healthier than chips.

items.definitionEn: cooked in hot oil
items.example: Fried eggs are quick to make for breakfast.

items.definitionEn: cooked over or under strong heat
items.example: Grilled fish with salad is a light evening meal.

items.definitionEn: cooked in an oven with fat, often for Sunday lunch
items.example: We had roast chicken and vegetables.

items.definitionEn: not cooked
items.example: Sushi is made with raw fish.

items.definitionEn: with a hot, strong flavour from spices
items.example: This curry is too spicy for my little brother.

items.definitionEn: having a sharp taste, like strong coffee or dark chocolate
items.example: Dark chocolate can taste quite bitter.

items.definitionEn: having an acid taste, like lemon or vinegar
items.example: The milk smells sour — do not drink it.

items.definitionEn: very pleasant to eat or drink
items.example: The homemade cake was absolutely delicious.

items.definitionEn: made at home, not bought in a shop
items.example: Homemade soup tastes better than tinned soup.

items.definitionEn: a medical problem caused by eating or touching something
items.example: Tell the waiter if you have a nut allergy.

items.definitionEn: to eat or drink less of something
items.example: The doctor told him to cut down on sweets.

items.definitionEn: extremely hungry
items.example: I skipped lunch, so I am starving now.

items.definitionEn: a small amount of food between meals
items.example: An apple is a healthier snack than crisps.
